newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria troops under fire over racist T-shirts.
newsitem.headline: Austria troops under fire over racist T-shirts.

text.p: Austrian military commanders launched an inquiry into the conduct of their troops in Bosnia on Tuesday following revelations that members of one platoon wore T-shirts bearing a racist slogan.

The shirts, inscribed with the name of the peacekeeping Implementation Force, IFOR, and the legend: "Wogs go quiet when our strong arm dictates. Heavy Platoon," have sparked a political row in a country painfully aware of its Nazi past.
A caricature of far-right Austrian Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider flexing his muscles, a workman's hammer slung across his shoulder, was also emblazoned across the vests.

Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend said number three platoon of Austria's transport corps, in Bosnia as part of the NATO-led peacekeeping operation, ordered 30 of the shirts from a Hungarian manufacturer.
"They were meant to evoke a team spirit. Our commanding officer gave the go-ahead," Austrian media quoted one of the soldiers as saying.
The environmentalist Greens drew attention to the shirts after spotting two Austrian soldiers wearing them on a Croatia to Vienna train at the weekend.
Fasslabend insisted that only a handful of soldiers were involved and said there was no evidence rightwing extremists were behind the platoon's choice of logo.

"One has to ask the question whether this foolishness is worthy of so much media attention, distorting the picture of our forces' achievements abroad," said the minister, a member of the conservative junior coalition partner the People's Party.
Brigadier Klaus Koehler, commander of Austria's IFOR troops in Bosnia, called the shirts "stupid and tasteless".
"They have been confiscated and we will initiate disciplinary proceedings," he told state television.
A military spokesman said the shirts were worn only in barracks or during home leave.
Some ruling Social Democrats appeared far from happy with the official response, however, and one parliamentarian said he planned to table a question on the issue.

"Racism is particularly offensive when it is practiced by people serving Austria abroad," said Social Democrat Wolfgang Riedler. "We cannot turn a blind eye to this. Fasslabend has to give parliament a full explanation."
Freedom Party general secretary Peter Westenthaler was alone in defending the soldiers.
Austria sent 268 soldiers earlier this year to handle transport in the Sarajevo area.
